title: Re-advertisement -Protection Officer – Return, Reintegration & Mixed Migration -P2P
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified Protection Officer

About the job

The Protection Officer is responsible for field-level coordination, implementation and quality assurance of DRC's SIDA P2P protection, return/reintegration and related Economic Recovery linkages in Bosaso and relevant Eastern Route return and transit locations in Puntland. The role supports timely, protection-sensitive delivery of DRC direct activities and field-level accompaniment of local partners across vulnerability screening/case management, PSS, IPA and referrals, route-based Protection Monitoring, reintegration follow-up, livelihoods linkages and systems strengthening.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

Protection services, case management and direct assistance


	Coordinate vulnerability screening and protection risk assessment for migrants and returnees and support safe, rights-based case management and referral follow-up in line with DRC SOPs, informed consent, confidentiality and Do No Harm.
	Provide field-level technical guidance to assigned DRC caseworkers and support quality of partner case-management/referral delivery as delegated; ensure GBV, Child Protection, trafficking and other specialized concerns are safely identified and referred.
	Coordinate approved IPA and other immediate protection support, and facilitate safe referrals to MHPSS, health, legal aid, shelter/housing, civil documentation, livelihoods and other specialized services based on assessed needs.


 PSS, return/reintegration and Economic Recovery linkages


	Coordinate/support delivery of structured individual and group PSS and appropriate referral to specialized MHPSS services.
	Support dignified reception, protection screening, information and counselling, access to hotline services, documentation, individualized reintegration planning and structured post-return follow-up, including through the Bosaso MRC and other P2P service points as relevant.
	Work closely with Economic Recovery colleagues and partners to link returnees to market-informed skills, employment/self-employment, business/start-up and financial-inclusion pathways, ensuring protection barriers and safeguarding considerations are integrated.


 Protection Monitoring, referral systems and evidence


	Coordinate regular community and route-based Protection Monitoring in assigned locations; provide day-to-day technical guidance to Protection Monitors/enumerators and ensure urgent protection risks and referral needs trigger appropriate response.
	Support service mapping and referral/RMS strengthening, monitor referral functionality, and contribute to the Ethiopia-Somalia cross-border case-management/legal-aid pilot in line with agreed consent, confidentiality and data-protection protocols.
	Use anonymized Protection Monitoring and referral trends to inform programme adaptation, reporting, validation and evidence/advocacy, keeping confidential case data separate from routine monitoring/MEAL datasets.


 Partner, government and stakeholder coordination


	Provide field-level technical accompaniment to KAALO, participate in joint monitoring with government counterparts and KAALO, and follow up agreed capacity-strengthening actions on Protection, referrals, PSS, Protection Monitoring and rights-based return/reintegration.
	Support existing government-led migration, referral and reintegration systems through joint monitoring, dialogue, practical coordination and on-the-job support, strengthening rather than creating parallel mechanisms.
	Coordinate with authorities, MRCs, service providers, community structures and humanitarian/protection actors, and support relevant reintegration, social-cohesion and stakeholder-engagement activities as assigned.


 Planning, monitoring, reporting and compliance


	Maintain field activity plans and monitor delivery against approved workplans, budgets, targets and programme-quality standards; identify implementation gaps and support timely corrective action.
	Coordinate with MEAL/IM, Economic Recovery, Partnerships/Grants, Finance and relevant programme/area teams; maintain accurate programme documentation and timely activity/technical reporting.
	Ensure implementation complies with DRC policies and donor requirements, safeguarding/PSEA/AAP commitments, core Protection principles, confidentiality and responsible data management.


About you

To be successful in this role we expect you to have:

Required 


	Minimum 3 years of relevant Protection experience in humanitarian, displacement or mixed-migration settings; experience in return/reintegration is strongly preferred.
	Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Psychology, Sociology, Human Rights, International Development, Peace and Conflict Studies, or a closely related field.
	Demonstrated experience in case management/referrals, PSS, Protection Monitoring and protection-sensitive direct assistance.
	Relevant training in Protect

title: INGO Group Programme Support Officer Readvertised
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly motivated INGO Group Programme support Officer for our operations in our Addis Ababa country Office.

(This is a re-advertisement. Applicants from previous rounds do not need to re-apply. 


Instruction for applicants:
All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English. Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered.


Overall purpose of the role 


	Oversee all aspects of administrative support at the INGO Group Secretariat office, ensuring efficient operations and procedures.
	 Implementation of administrative policies at the office.
	Develop systems that contribute to improve the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of the administrative operations.
	Bridge programmatic support and communications functions, ensuring members are well-informed, external stakeholders see the Group’s impact, and thematic initiatives receive operational support.


Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

Facilities Office management


	Ensure all office infrastructures are appropriate, safe and functioning (i.e. security system, health and safety, communications, etc.)
	Oversee all aspects of office maintenance and cleanliness.
	In conjunction with the DRC and INGO safety team, ensure safety and security issues for the general security of the office.
	Coordinates with DRC administration on office space and communication materials
	Coordinate handover of leased properties and ensure security deposits are refunded on timely basis.
	Ensure repairs and maintenance of facilities in compliance with DRC standards and procedures.
	Manage the administration team to ensure overall efficiency.


Administrative support


	Ensure all INGO GROUP payments are done on timely basis.
	Ensure meetings for the INGO GROUP Country Directors and INGO GROUP Steering Committee are organized and other administrative support as may be required.
	Keeps and updates the INGO GROUP Team calendar, vehicle utilization log and Steering Committee calendar.
	Drafts minutes of meetings where appropriate.
	Any other duties as requested by Manager.
	Support as may be necessary the efforts of INGO GROUP working groups – HR, Duty of Care, Engagement and Comms, and Humanitarian Leads. 


Logistics and finance


	Acts as the focal point for all logistics, supply chain and procurement matters within the INGO GROUP secretariat and liaises with DRC’s related department accordingly.
	Prepares payment requests, expense reports and procurement requests in accordance with DRC systems and procedures.
	Organizes the logistical aspects of preparing meetings, workshops, trainings and events for the INGO Group. This includes booking meeting halls, purchasing stationery and other materials; liaising with DRC administration department on visas and hotel bookings for external participants; coordinating with hotels and suppliers; submitting payment requests in a timely manner and ensuring payments are done on time.
	Liaises with DRC Supply Chain and fleet manager on the use of the dedicated INGO vehicle.


IT and Databases management


	Updates the INGO GROUP members and external stakeholders’ databases.
	Liaises with DRC IT department, at country and HQ levels, to ensure to update and functionalities of the INGO Group mailing lists and groups.
	Manages creation of, admissions to and good functioning of the INGO Groups.


Communications support 


	Lead internal and external communications including newsletters, press releases, and digital platforms.
	Support coordination of working groups thematic discussions and events
	Manage visibility (website, briefing notes etc)
	Assist in reporting and donor engagement ensuring timely and accurate documentation.
	Provide basic programmatic support tot thematic initiatives


Experience and technical competencies:


	At least 3 years' experience in administration and programme support in an international NGO in a similar role at mid-management level.
	Knowledge of travel and immigration procedures.
	Experience in basic database management and event organization.
	Advanced English proficiency
	Fluency in local language


 EDUCATION: (include certificates, licenses, etc.)


	University degree or equivalent professional qualification


LANGUAGE: (indicate Fluency level)


	English (fluent)

title: Protection Manager
Head of Programme
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified Head of Programme for Congo 

Danish Refugee Council is a leading protection agency pursuing our mandate to protect and promote durable solutions to displacement-affected populations based on humanitarian principles. In East Africa and the Great Lakes, DRC has operational presence in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, and Uganda. 

In the DR Congo, DRC has been involved in humanitarian aid since 2009. Initially working in Province Orientale, DRC gradually extended its reach to North Kivu and Ituri provinces. The sectors of intervention for DRC in the country are provision of Emergency Response, Protection (including GBV and child protection), Economic Recovery, Shelter and WASH. DRC is currently responding to the Ebola outbreak as this is unfolding in Ituri province where DRC has a longstanding presence.

 

About the job

Provide strategic direction, leadership and oversight of DRC’s country programme, ensuring coherent strategy, high programme quality, effective departmental management and sustainable funding. Lead country-level programme development and support accountable implementation through Area Managers and Project Managers. As a member of the Senior Management Team, the HoP oversees a multi-sector portfolio spanning emergency response, early recovery and resilience in eastern DR Congo, including consortia led by DRC, and works closely with the Head of Support Services and the Head of Safety to balance programme excellence, cost efficiency and safety.

 

Main Responsibilities

Programme Strategy & Development


	Lead and periodically review the Country Programme Plan, Theory of Change and sector/geographic priorities; translate strategy into clear departmental workplans.
	Coordinate an integrated, multi-sector approach across Protection, Economic Recovery, WASH, Education and other sectors; ensure the centrality of protection, safe programming, access and adherence to humanitarian principles; uphold technical standards and safeguarding.
	Promote cash and market-based programming (including multi-purpose and emergency cash) and link emergency response with early recovery and durable solutions.
	Drive innovative programme design with the SMT, in line with DRC global and regional strategies.


Programme Coordination

	Lead the Country Office Business Development Plan, donor mapping, opportunity pipeline, strategic partnerships and funding proposals, including ECHO HIP processes.
	Coordinate programme approaches across Protection, Economic Recovery, WASH, Education and other sectors; uphold technical standards and safeguarding.
	Maintain programme risks and mitigation actions in the Country Office Risk Register; analyze options and take timely decisions within delegated authority.
	Provide concise, decision-oriented updates to SMT and coordinate priorities with Area Offices, Finance, HR, Supply Chain, Safety, Regional Hub and HQ.
	Ensure effective and transparent planning and use of financial resources (budget follow-up, burn rates) in compliance with DRC and donor rules; keep programme staff updated on donor regulations.


Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability & Learning (MEAL)


	Provide strategic oversight to PDQM; ensure Grants and MEAL have clear strategies, workplans, quality controls, donor reporting and learning systems.
	Ensure monitoring systems produce quality evidence that is used for programme adjustment and accountability to affect populations; document and share lessons learned and good practices internally and externally.


Fundraising, Proposal Development & Reporting


	Lead the Country Office Business Development Plan, donor mapping, opportunity pipeline, strategic partnerships and funding proposals, including ECHO HIP processes.
	Oversee timely, quality concept notes, proposals, budgets and donor reports with Grants, Finance and field teams, in line with DRC and donor requirements.
